comments.body:
REFUTED by on-box evidence — see bug df2c-e4b8-496d-4698 (strained-bare-turnstone).

The auto-deploy / mid-review-restart hypothesis does not hold. Container recreation times for compose-review-bot-1 were 2026-08-01T23:25:04, 08-02T00:00:22, 08-02T03:59:28, 08-02T05:37:03 UTC. The four coverage-gap votes landed at 23:39:03, 00:22:11, 04:46:53 and 16:41:48 — each strictly INSIDE a single container's lifetime (1208's container 4bd32a5e5170 had been up 12h and kept reviewing afterwards). A SIGTERM would also not have emitted the 'git fetch ... timed out after 300s' line that each failure did emit.

The real mechanism is a transient GitHub git-fetch hang (reproduced: 2/25 runs of the exact fetch inside the container hung >320s, the other 23 took 1-3s) burning the 300s _GIT_TIMEOUT, which adapter.py:207-211 converts into a vote-bearing BLOCK, which reconcile.py:210 then treats as 'already voted' and skips forever.

This ticket's second half — 'fail-NO-VOTE instead of fail-closed for retryable conditions' — is the correct fix and is carried in df2c. The 'hourly cadence' half is not needed for this defect.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
DESIGN DECISIONS (settled with maintainer @JoeOakhartNava, to be implemented). Landing order: this ticket FIRST, then bb9b.

Change 1 — cadence: rebar-autodeploy.timer 2min -> HOURLY. Document the staleness tradeoff AND the on-demand escape hatch (`systemctl start rebar-autodeploy.service`) in BOTH the unit file and the runbook.

Change 2 — the vote/no-vote split:
* Retryable -> NO VOTE (leave the change vote-less so the backfill reconciler re-drives it): review-error, llm-unavailable, scanner, and process-teardown-mid-review.
* Terminal -> VOTE -1:
  - finding (unchanged);
  - gate-disabled — a configuration state that yields the IDENTICAL result forever, so a no-vote would make backfill retry it forever (the invisible-infinite-loop this ticket warns against). It votes -1;
  - indeterminate — a genuine concluded "could not determine" is a real fail-closed veto, so it votes -1 (terminal).
  Both gate-disabled and indeterminate remain manually re-triggerable via bb9b (indeterminate is eligible there; gate-disabled is refused).

Teardown-vs-conclusion boundary (the critical discriminator): app.py shutdown/drain sets a shutdown/cancel flag (cancel scope) that the voter checks; a CancelledError raised during drain is treated as retryable NO-VOTE rather than falling through to the fail-closed -1 conversion. A verdict that actually reached an indeterminate conclusion still votes.

Bounded-retry escalation (AC6): after N vote-less attempts on the SAME revision, escalate by BOTH casting the -1 (so a human / bb9b sees it) AND emitting the CloudWatch metric.

Constraints preserved: (1) vote-less must remain unsubmittable — verify no degraded mode (RECONCILE_DEGRADED) turns "no vote" into submittable; (2) genuinely vote-less — nothing provisional posted on the change, or backfill re-suppresses.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Design review decisions (operator-approved 2026-08-02):

1. Change 1 is REVISED from 'hourly cadence' to the pattern zero-downtime OSS deployments converge on: QUIESCE, don't rarefy.
   a. Deploy only when the image/main actually changed — the autodeploy service must no-op when there is nothing new to deploy (this also addresses the unexplained ch1193 collision, where no main commit landed in the review window: a redeploy with no new commit should never have restarted the container).
   b. A 20-minute drain is APPROVED: size stop_grace_period (and the container's shutdown drain) to cover the measured max review duration (~911s observed; 20min gives headroom) rather than only the 150s store-write tail. This is the Kubernetes terminationGracePeriodSeconds/preStop pattern — the deploy waits for in-flight work instead of killing it. The 2-minute timer cadence can then stay (a deploy that quiesces is safe at any cadence), though hourly remains acceptable as belt-and-braces.

2. Change 2 (fail-NO-VOTE for retryable) confirmed as specified — it matches how Zuul (jobs interrupted by executor restart are retried without reporting) and Prow (evicted jobs rescheduled) behave; the bounded-retry escalation mirrors Zuul's RETRY_LIMIT. On the open 'indeterminate' judgement call: by those systems' semantics, a review that RAN TO COMPLETION and concluded 'cannot determine' is a result -> VOTE -1 (terminal); only teardown/infra paths are vote-less.

3. Harmonize with bb9b: the bounded-retry state (attempt counter per revision) must be a shared mechanism — bb9b's contributor trigger acts as 'reset the retry budget and re-drive' on the same state, not a parallel retry system. Land this ticket first; design the retry-bound storage so bb9b can reuse it.

compiled_state.description:
# Stop auto-deploy killing live code reviews: quiesce via a full-review drain window, and fail-NO-VOTE for retryable conditions

## Problem

The continuous auto-deploy restarts the review-bot container while a code review is in
flight, and the interrupted review casts a fail-closed `LLM-Review -1`. That vote then
BLOCKS the automatic recovery which already exists, so every occurrence costs a human
re-trigger. Observed FOUR times in one session (changes 1132/1189/1193/1208; three of four
had a `main` commit land mid-review; measured review durations 260-911s against a 45s
drain).

### What the code actually does today (verified against source)

* `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` ALREADY deploys only on change: `changed()` diffs
  deployed-sha..target per path-class and rebuilds the bot only when `BOT_PATHS` /
  `SECRETS_PATHS` changed (autodeploy.sh:219-230). "Deploy only when the image changes" is
  already true — the unexplained 1193 collision needs a different explanation (candidates:
  a SECRETS_PATHS-only refresh, or a backoff retry of a previously-failed target;
  investigate during implementation and record on this ticket).
* The shutdown drain ALREADY waits for the in-flight review: the lifespan does
  `await queue.join()` bounded by `shutdown_drain_seconds()` (app.py:117) and the worker
  marks the queue item done only after `review_and_vote` returns. The defect is purely the
  CONSTANT: `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS = 45` (config.py:42) versus
  `DEFAULT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1200` (config.py:30). A deploy landing mid-review
  times out the drain at 45s, cancels the worker, and the teardown-corrupted review
  fail-closes a `-1`.
* The backfill reconciler (`reconcile.py`) re-drives any CURRENT revision with NO
  `LLM-Review` vote, on startup and every 300s. Casting the fail-closed `-1` makes the
  change invisible to it — the veto disables the recovery designed for this failure.

## Change 1 — quiesce: size the drain to a full review (operator-approved 20 min)

Raise `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS` from 45 to 1200 (= the per-review timeout — the
principled bound: the drain exists to let the in-flight review finish, and the review is
already wall-clock-bounded by `REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`). Resize
`stop_grace_period` in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` per its existing derivation
(drain + store write-lock budget + push reconcile lock): 1200 + 60 + 45 -> 1320s, updating
the derivation comment.
`tests/unit/test_review_bot.py::test_reviewbot_stop_grace_period_covers_an_in_flight_store_write`
reads both values from source and enforces the relationship — it must pass unmodified.

Cost when no review is in flight: none (`queue.join()` returns immediately on an empty
queue). Cost when one is in flight: the deploy waits for it — that is the point (the
Kubernetes terminationGracePeriodSeconds/preStop pattern). The 2-minute timer cadence
stays: a deploy that quiesces is safe at any cadence, and autodeploy already no-ops on an
unchanged target.

## Change 2 — fail-NO-VOTE for retryable coverage gaps, with a bounded escalation

Matches how Zuul (jobs interrupted by an executor restart are retried without reporting)
and Prow (evicted jobs are rescheduled) behave; the bounded retry mirrors Zuul's
RETRY_LIMIT.

* `adapter.code_review_decision` already classifies every non-PASS outcome
  (`_TAG_SUFFIXES` / `_coverage_gap_reason`). Thread the machine-readable sub-reason out
  of `_block` as a new `gap_reason` key on the decision dict (None for PASS/finding).
* In `voter.review_and_vote`, when the decision is a coverage-gap BLOCK with a RETRYABLE
  `gap_reason` — `review-error`, `llm-unavailable`, `scanner`, `gate-disabled` — do NOT
  post the vote. Record the attempt in a new `review_attempts` table beside the dedup
  ledger (`dedup.py` SQLite, keyed `(change_id, revision)`), emit a distinct greppable
  `REVIEW_RETRY_DEFERRED` marker, and return. The change stays vote-less, so the EXISTING
  backfill reconciler re-drives it within `RECONCILE_INTERVAL_SECONDS` — no reconciler
  change needed.
* `indeterminate` is TERMINAL (vote the `-1`): by CI-system semantics a review that RAN TO
  COMPLETION and concluded "cannot establish coverage" is a result, not an interruption.
  `finding` is unchanged. The merge-path `_merge_coverage_gap_decision` keeps its current
  fail-closed vote in this ticket: it deliberately gets NO `gap_reason` key (its REST
  failures are pre-review setup; revisit separately if it recurs), and the voter's
  deferral protocol keys strictly on `gap_reason` being present and retryable.
* Bounded escalation: when `review_attempts` reaches the cap (new
  `RETRYABLE_GAP_MAX_ATTEMPTS`, default 3, env-overridable via `ReceiverConfig`), cast the
  fail-closed `-1` with the original reason's tag plus an appended "automatic retries
  exhausted" note (tag VOCABULARY unchanged — the tag test keeps passing), and emit the
  existing `VOTER_ERROR` marker so the `rebar/host:voter_errors` alarm surface fires.
  The attempts store is deliberately shaped for ticket bb9b's contributor re-trigger to
  RESET (shared retry budget). Reset semantics: `reset_attempts(change_id, revision)`
  DELETES the row (no status flags, no zeroed counters left behind) — after a reset the
  store is indistinguishable from "never attempted". The attempt is recorded (INSERT/
  increment) BEFORE the deferral `return`; a SQLite failure on that write is caught and
  logged as `VOTER_ERROR` and the deferral still returns vote-less (an uncounted attempt
  only delays escalation by one cycle — fail-open on the counter, never on the vote).
* Teardown mid-review needs no separate discriminator: the deferral decision happens
  before any vote POST, so a teardown-corrupted review that fail-closes as `review-error`
  is deferred vote-less, and with Change 1 the cancel almost never lands mid-review at
  all.

### Constraints (both verified as part of implementation)

1. **No silent-pass hole.** Vote-less stays unsubmittable (submit REQUIRES `LLM-Review +1`);
   assert no reconciler degraded mode turns "no vote" into "submittable".
2. **Genuinely vote-less.** The deferral posts NOTHING to the change (no provisional
   comment), or the reconciler's no-vote pre-filter would be re-suppressed.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/review_bot/config.py` — drain default 45 -> 1200; new
  `RETRYABLE_GAP_MAX_ATTEMPTS`.
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` — `stop_grace_period` 150s -> 1320s + derivation
  comment.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py` — `gap_reason` on the decision dict.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py` — defer-not-vote for retryable gaps + bounded
  escalation.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/dedup.py` — the `review_attempts` table: `record_attempt` /
  `attempt_count` keyed `(change_id, revision)`, and `reset_attempts` = DELETE the row.
  This table is SEPARATE from the existing `voted` table; the deferred path writes ONLY
  to `review_attempts`, never to `voted`.
- `docs/env-vars.md` — regenerate for the new env var (the committed registry is drift-
  gated by `tests/unit/test_gen_env_registry.py::test_check_mode_clean_against_committed_tree`).
- `docs/review-policy.md` — document the retryable/terminal split and the escalation.
- Tests in `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py` (see below).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS` is 1200 and compose `stop_grace_period` is
      1320s; `test_reviewbot_stop_grace_period_covers_an_in_flight_store_write` passes
      unmodified.
- [ ] AC2: a coverage-gap decision with `gap_reason` in {review-error, llm-unavailable,
      scanner, gate-disabled} casts NO vote, records an attempt, and posts nothing to the
      change, and emits the greppable `REVIEW_RETRY_DEFERRED` marker — asserted by a
      unit test per reason.
- [ ] AC3: `indeterminate` and `finding` still cast the `-1`, and PASS still casts the
      `+1` — asserted by tests (no behaviour change for terminal outcomes).
- [ ] AC4: the Nth (default 3rd) consecutive retryable failure on the same
      `(change_id, revision)` casts the fail-closed `-1` with the "retries exhausted" note
      and emits `VOTER_ERROR` — asserted by a test; the cap is env-overridable.
- [ ] AC5: the deferred path leaves the change eligible for the backfill reconciler — no
      row in the `voted` table and no Gerrit vote (the `review_attempts` row from AC2 is
      expected and does NOT suppress re-drive) — asserted by a test driving the
      reconciler over a deferred change.
- [ ] AC6: `docs/review-policy.md` documents the retryable/terminal split, the bound, and
      the escalation surface.
- [ ] AC7: `docs/env-vars.md` is regenerated and committed (its drift-gate test passes),
      and `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the review-bot test module pass.

## Testing / Verification

From the worktree venv:
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -q`
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint && env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`

## Relationship to bb9b

`bb9b-608f-0183-4ca5` (lands second) gives contributors a manual re-trigger for any
remaining `-1` that is not a real finding — including this ticket's escalated `-1` —
implemented as "reset the shared `review_attempts` budget + force re-review". This ticket
deliberately shapes the attempts store for that reuse.

file_impact.reason: cadence 2min -> hourly; document the staleness tradeoff and the on-demand deploy escape hatch
split retryable coverage-gap reasons (no vote, leave for backfill) from a real finding (vote -1); bounded-retry escalation
shutdown/drain path must mark a torn-down review as retryable rather than letting it reach the fail-closed conversion
tag table must state which coverage-gap reasons cast a vote and which leave the change vote-less
prove interrupted review casts no vote, backfill re-drives it, and no degraded mode makes vote-less submittable
